description: One GGUF artifact serves llama.cpp natively (and vLLM via the GGUF path). The lane's own harness is llama-perplexity, which is why its KL evaluator is an adapter rather than the resident one — the artifact cannot be materialised into a torch model without leaving the format under test.
wired_architectures_note: hy_v3 is the architecture whose shipped artifact came off this lane. Moved here from tests/test_profile_export_lanes.py's GGUF_WIRED on 2026-09-03: the roster is a decision and belongs beside the lane it decides, not in a test that names two lanes and would miss a third.

gates.description: Load + greedy generate, run inline by run-pipeline.sh's GGUF branch — the one lane whose load smoke is already in the pipeline, because its runtime is a binary and not an importable package.
llama-server exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so the same endpoint-agnostic ship gate applies unchanged.
The lane's native KL harness: base logits saved once from the bf16 skeleton, then per artifact.
PPL from the same harness; Mean PPL(Q) is parsed from the same output as the KL.

kl_evaluator.note: Wraps `llama-perplexity --kl-divergence-base` behind the validate_assignments_kl interface: (mean, per_sequence, stats) with the gold lane's key names. per_sequence is EMPTY — llama-perplexity reports aggregate quantiles, not per-sequence values — so stats carries kl_tail_domain='aggregate' and the tail keys come from its own quantiles rather than being recomputed.

notes: This evaluator is what makes --packed-role-split measurable: the role split hard-gates on supports_per_role_expert_schemes, which only gguf declares, and the lane previously had no validated-frontier evaluator at all (D26).
GGUF cost/render lockstep is keyed on PRISMAQUANT_GGUF_IMATRIX: the cost render applies the imatrix exactly when the export does (§4.7).
